blurb: Louis Le Blanc de Beaulieu - Sedan Theological Theses, newly rendered from the 1675 London Latin. Covers De Theologia through Angelorum & Hominum Sanctorum Cultu Romana I-LXXVII and Pars Secunda (Reformata) I-CI, De Primi Hominis Immortalitate I-XXXV, De Justitia Primi Hominis I-LIX, De Libero Hominis Arbitrio in genere I-XLVIII, De Libero Hominis Arbitrio absolute & in se spectato (Scholae Romanae doctrina I-XLIX; Pars Tertia I-XLIII), the theses on reconciling divine concurrence with human freedom I-LIX, on human freedom and divine foreknowledge I-XLIV, and on human freedom and the divine decrees, Part One (middle knowledge) I-LXV, Part Two (the Roman doctors) I-XXXVI and Part Three (the Reformed) I-LI, and on how fallen man's free choice stands toward saving good (I-LX), and on the necessity of grace for moral good in fallen man (Pars Prior I-LIII; Pars Posterior, the Protestant doctrine, I-LIX), and on the various distinctions and senses of grace in the Roman School (I-LXX) and in the Reformed Schools (I-XLIX), and on the Roman School's division of grace into sufficient and efficacious (I-CXLV, complete), and on the Protestant doctrine of that distinction, the Lutherans of the Augsburg Confession, the Remonstrants, and the Reformed who subscribe to Dort, with the Reformed debate on how grace moves the will, Le Blanc's concluding comparisons and an appendix on the Socinians (I-LXXXVIII, complete), and on whether and how far man can fulfil the Law by Christ's grace (I-LI, complete), and on the truth of the good works the regenerate do by Christ's grace (I-XVIII). Not the collected folio.
era_note: Le Blanc wrote in the mid-seventeenth century as Reformed professor at the Academy of Sedan. This is not a patristic work. It is a public-domain Latin Reformed retrieval on the same Fathers-site pipeline. The 1675 Pitt folio is Public Domain Mark 1.0. Do not treat the site as ante-Nicene only.
